analysis.title: "Memory Meltdown": Goldman Finds Fast Money Piled Into Nasdaq At The Top... And Asset Managers Haven't Blinked Yet
key_insights: GS Memory and AI Semiconductor baskets fell 9.3% and 6.7% during Oct 5-12. Catalysts included CXMT reporting 'key progress' on a new cell architecture to boost memory density, which competes with SK Hynix.
GS Memory basket started a year ago near 600, peaked near 2,675 in late June and sits near 1,900. That is more than triple a year ago and about 25% below the June peak.
Hynix was already 45% off its June high before the CXMT shock. Per GS's TMT desk, Samsung, Hynix, Kioxia, WDC, STX, MU and Sandisk fell 5-15% overnight.

The trigger was CXMT's unsubstantiated claim (per Bloomberg) that its new 4F² DRAM architecture gets it there before Samsung and Hynix despite US sanctions on top-end ASML tools. Elon Musk commented that China's ability to scale is often greater than the rest of the world combined.
Nasdaq 3M funding versus Fed Funds richened, but Nasdaq's premium to S&P reversed from its local peak, notably on Oct 12 index weakness. Levered longs initially appeared unconcerned before pivoting.

Nasdaq 3M funding is roughly 76bps over Fed Funds (read off the chart), about double its March lows and below the roughly 124bps June peak that coincided with the memory peak. Nasdaq's funding premium over S&P hit roughly 7bps in early October, the top of its range for the year, before rolling over.

CFTC data: 'Other' (fast money) Nasdaq futures gross longs on Oct 6 were at 1-year highs in notional terms and as a share of open interest. GS says at least one category potentially reduced recently implemented length. Short-term correlations versus Memory and AI Semis were positive.
Other gross longs were roughly $9.6B on Oct 6, up from about $3B in early July, and about 5.4% of open interest versus about 1.4% in late June (approximate chart reads).
Asset Manager gross longs on Oct 6 showed no significant relationship with the Memory or AI Semi barometers, so whether the selloff affects their sentiment remains debatable per GS.

Asset Manager gross longs in Nasdaq futures were roughly $70B on Oct 6, near the roughly $71B June record and up from about $44B in late March (approximate). The article argues this is the next potential seller.
GS calculated Micron alone would deliver 19% of the S&P 500's Q3 earnings growth. Nanya printed an 85.7% gross margin.
Pictet's Jon Withaar told Bloomberg memory names 'have become value names, cheap at current earnings' and that retail and fast money hedge funds do not chase value.
GS's Korea team flags whether memory supply stays tight into 2028 as the key question ahead of Samsung's Oct 29 call. GS sees CXMT's DRAM supply reaching half of Hynix's by 2028.
GS desks expect the semi dip to get bought, with ASML on Oct 15 and TSMC on Thursday (Oct 15) as the first tests. The Korean leading indicator is down about 30%.
